s1.syndrome_frame: Abdominal pain and mass with acute exacerbation
salient_findings: Palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen
Large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum on ultrasound
Large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall on endoscopy
key_facts: 63-year-old woman
Insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion
Nausea
Episode of intense acute abdominal pain
No hematemesis or melena
Untreated dyslipidemia
Well-controlled hypertension on methyldopa
Smoker of ten cigarettes per day
No family history of cancer
Normal physical examination except for abdominal mass
Normal laboratory tests, including complete blood count
No anemia
Abdominal ultrasound showed large echogenic mass in gastric antrum
Endoscopy revealed large submucosal bulging mass in posterior gastric wall
Biopsy attempts failed to sample submucosal mass
Ulcer biopsies showed only necrotic mucosa
Contrast-enhanced CT showed well-defined, homogeneous, oval mass arising from posterior gastric wall

trace.fact: Palpable, movable mass in the upper abdomen

rule_in.why: it is typically palpable and movable

rule_out.why: it is less likely to present as a palpable movable mass

trace.fact: Large echogenic mass in the gastric antrum on ultrasound

rule_in.why: it is most commonly associated with large echogenic masses in the gastric antrum

trace.fact: Large submucosal bulging mass in the posterior gastric wall on endoscopy

rule_in.why: it is commonly associated with submucosal masses in the stomach

rule_out.why: it is typically small and has a characteristic appearance on endoscopy

trace.fact: Insidious upper abdominal pain unrelated to food ingestion

rule_in.why: it often presents with non-specific abdominal pain

rule_out.why: Lipomas are typically asymptomatic and less likely to cause pain

rule_in.why: it is most closely associated with nausea

trace.fact: Episode of intense acute abdominal pain

rule_in.why: it can cause acute abdominal pain due to potential rupture or bleeding
the fact is equally compatible with all candidates

rule_out.why: it often presents with hematemesis or melena
